answer: A stake-weighted reputation trellis makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent identity must lock a bond that vests slowly, like an orchard that only bears fruit after seasons of honest work, while a willow-like flexible slashing rule bends but never breaks under coordinated fake identities. Creating thousands of sock-puppet agents requires locking real capital per identity, and any proven fraud burns the bond, so attackers pay more to fake the network than they can extract from it.
